commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Handle OOM when copying encodingName in XML_ParserReset

When XML_ParserReset(parser, encodingName) is called with a non-NULL
encodingName, parserInit() invokes copyString() to allocate and store
the protocol encoding name. If memory allocation fails, copyString()
returns NULL.

Unlike parserCreate() and XML_SetEncoding(), which both check
(encodingName && ! parser->m_protocolEncodingName) and fail cleanly,
XML_ParserReset() previously ignored this allocation failure and returned
XML_TRUE. This silently dropped the requested encoding, leaving
m_protocolEncodingName as NULL while reporting success to the caller.

Check for this allocation failure in XML_ParserReset(), set
parser->m_errorCode to XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY, and return XML_FALSE.
Also add a unit test test_alloc_reset_encoding in alloc_tests.c.

While at it, free the memory backing a still installed unknown encoding
right away in XML_ParserReset(), before the tag stack, entity lists and
bindings are recycled, so that the remainder of the function operates on
a parser that no longer references the encoding of the previous run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

lib: Call unknown encoding release before teardown

The application-defined release callback receives no arguments beyond
the data pointer that the application itself supplied, so it has no way
of learning anything about the teardown going on around it. Callbacks
routinely reach back into the parser, e.g. to log the position at which
the unknown encoding was installed.

Move the call to callUnknownEncodingRelease() in XML_ParserFree() to the
top of the function, ahead of any parser state being freed or reset.
Also let XML_ParserReset() run the release before the bindings are
recycled, for symmetry.

Signed-off-by: Junki Lee <junkilee80@gmail.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
Regime incomplete_fix: at the batch base (main), both XML_ParserFree() and XML_ParserReset() FREE() the unknown-encoding memory (m_unknownEncodingMem, which backs parser->m_encoding) *before* invoking the application's XML_Encoding.release callback, so any parser-API call made from inside that release callback dereferences a freed ENCODING (heap-use-after-free). The real maintenance window fixes this in commit 3fbfd673; the case re-opens the hole in XML_ParserReset() only, and only through the composition of two edited commits:
(1) ff4dc437 (edited) keeps its real OOM-handling change for encodingName and in addition relocates the teardown line 'FREE(parser, parser->m_unknownEncodingMem)' from the bottom of XML_ParserReset() (right before the release call) to the very top, directly after the m_parentParser guard. On its own this is a pure relocation of a free that introduces no new ordering: the free-before-release order already existed at the base, and the later real fix still runs the release first.
(2) 3fbfd673 (edited) performs the release-before-teardown fix in XML_ParserFree() exactly as the real commit does (hoisted to the top of the function), and in XML_ParserReset() lifts the release call only a few lines, from after moveToFreeBindingList() to just after the moveEntityList() calls. In the layout this commit's parent actually has in the original history (free still down at the bottom, immediately below the release), that small lift is itself a complete fix: release runs before the free.
The defect exists only when both edits are read together: because edit (1) moved the FREE() above the entity/binding moves, the fixed anchor where edit (2) deposits the release call now sits *below* the free, so the final XML_ParserReset() runs FREE(m_unknownEncodingMem) first and callUnknownEncodingRelease() second. The callback is still invoked with parser->m_encoding dangling, and any parser query from inside it (XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64 etc.) reads freed heap memory.
Why the fix is non-local: reverting either edit alone removes the bug. Restoring the original ff4dc437 (edit 1 reverted) puts the free back below moveToFreeBindingList(), i.e. below where edit (2) placed the release, so release precedes free and the tree is secure (verified: rc=0). Restoring the original 3fbfd673 (edit 2 reverted) hoists the release to the very top of XML_ParserReset(), above the relocated free, so the tree is secure again (verified: rc=0). A correct repair therefore has to reason about both commits at once: either the release must be hoisted above the free's *current* (relocated) position, or the free must be kept below the release call; patching either single diff in isolation - e.g. applying the 'real' 3fbfd673 hunk that merely swaps two adjacent lines - leaves nothing to swap, because the two lines are no longer adjacent once ff4dc437's edit has moved the free away.
Both edited commits remain benign maintenance: the tree builds and the project's full test suite passes on the resulting tip when AddressSanitizer is off; each commit still accomplishes its stated purpose (OOM handling for encodingName in XML_ParserReset; calling the unknown-encoding release callback before teardown).

pocs.entry_point: api:XML_ParserReset (public libexpat API; probe drives XML_ParserCreate/XML_SetUnknownEncodingHandler/XML_Parse/XML_ParserReset/XML_ParserFree and calls XML_GetCurrentLineNumber64 from the release callback)
